text.p: Seamico Securities said on Tuesday that it recommended investors buy shares of Berli Jucker Plc due to the company's diversity and because it will not be affected by a slowdown in Thai exports.

"We continue to be bullish on BJC, given its strong exposure to both the consumer sector and the rush towards investment in the country's infrastructure," Seamico said in a report. "BJC is also a defensive stock and will be unaffected by the present slowdown in the Thai export sector.
Seamico said Berli Jucker's second quarter performance, announced on Monday, was in line with forcasts.
"The 12 percent sales increase was reasonable considering the volume of sales and BJC's diverse range of products," Seamico said.
Berli Jucker reported a net profit of 152 million baht or 2.64 baht per share in the second quarter compared to 126 million baht or 2.18 a share the same period in 1995.
Seamico said Berli Jucker's 55 percent owned unit, Cellox Paper, will attain better margins in the short term.
The company's wholly-owned Siam Snack is also expected to benefit in 1997 from projections of more than 50 percent growth for the snack industry.
Berli Jucker's 60-percent owned Thai Scandic Steel is still making losses, but it is expected to break even this year and make a profit from 1997 onwards.
Seamico said at 91.50 baht per share, Berli Jucker is trading and 8.9 times 1996 and 7.8 times 1997 earnings.
Berli Jucker was up 1.00 baht at 92.50 in late trade on Tuesday.
